question: Can chained-S3 SAT decomposition with a Frobenius-invariant (union) factor base decide m = 5 and m = 6 relations on Koblitz curves at n = 23, 29, 31, 37 and 41 within a 600 s cell cap scaled to the m = 4 root-table cost, and at n = 83 with the 180 s cap of n83_msweep_20261024 lifted tenfold to 1800 s; and what does a decided query cost?

claims.text: For each engine (chain-s3-orbit and chain-s3), at n = 23 (k0n23) the m = 5 and m = 6 public union:2 cells decide (all four queries SAT or proved UNSAT) inside the 600 s process cap.
claims.if_supported: The chained-S3 union-base line produces its first measured m >= 5 decided cells; their seconds per query are the first price of the line, to be compared with the m = 4 root-table figure.
claims.if_not_supported: Falsified for an engine if either of its two k0n23 cells caps or is undecided: at the smallest registered curve that engine does not decide m >= 5 inside 600 s single-threaded, and K2/K4 are read accordingly. The two engines are reported separately; the claim holds only if it holds for both.

claims.text: For each engine, decided-query seconds grow at least geometrically with n at fixed (m, S), such that every m = 6 public cell at n = 37 and n = 41 (S = 2, 3) hits the 600 s cap.
claims.if_supported: Cost per query rises past the Part A cap by n = 37; the curve gives the n at which each (m, S) leaves reach.
claims.if_not_supported: Falsified by any decided m = 6 public cell at n = 37 or 41, or by a non-positive log-slope between consecutive decided n at fixed (m, S). A cell skipped by the stopping rule is not measured, and K2 is then supported only on the measured cells (verdict supported_partial).

claims.text: In every decided planted cell, for both engines, the planted relation is recovered: every query returns a witness that is re-added in the curve group and equals the target (4 of 4 in Part A, 1 of 1 in Part B).
claims.if_supported: The instrument finds a relation that exists at each decided planted cell; public verdicts there are informative.
claims.if_not_supported: Any decided planted cell with a proved_unsat verdict or an unverified witness invalidates that cell's planted and public records and that engine at that (m, n, S); K4 and K5 are then not evaluable for it.

claims.text: At n = 83 (n83k1, a = 1 pinned fixture), for each engine, every m = 5 and m = 6 public cell (S = 2, 3) stays undecided at the 1800 s cap, which with one query per cell process is a per-query cap; the tenfold lift does not change the n83_msweep verdict.
claims.if_supported: The n = 83 m >= 5 chained line is capped at 1800 s as at 180 s; with K5 this is the kill criterion.
claims.if_not_supported: Falsified by any decided n = 83 public cell at m = 5 or 6: the 180 s verdict was a cap artefact and the line stays open at n = 83.

claims.text: For each engine, no decided public cell at n >= 31 (Part A) or at n = 83 (Part B) has seconds per decided query below 188 s, the m = 4 root-table parity threshold (n83 K1107 complete DLPs took 175-188 s), so the m >= 5 chained line stays behind m = 4. Stated plainly: Part A keeps 4 trials under a 600 s process cap, so a decided Part A cell proves at most 150 s per query; a decided Part A cell at n >= 31 therefore falsifies K5 by construction, and otherwise K5 stays untested on capped cells (a cap is a censored observation, not a cost above 188 s). Part B runs one query per process under 1800 s, so a Part B cell is the only place a per-query cost above 188 s can be observed.
claims.if_supported: No decided m >= 5 chained cell undercuts one m = 4 root-table DLP. When no cell at n >= 31 decides, K5 holds vacuously and is reported as such: capped Part A cells show only that four queries together exceed 600 s, which does not test 188 s.
claims.if_not_supported: Falsified by any decided public cell at n >= 31 with seconds per query below 188 s; every decided Part A cell at n >= 31 does so (at most 150 s per query), so Part A decisions at n >= 31 falsify K5 by construction. The line then has a measured improvement over the m = 4 parity point and is reported as the distance remaining, not as a pass.

claims.text: Kill criterion for the high-arity Koblitz line: K4 and K5 both supported for both engines, with K3 not falsified.
claims.if_supported: The high-arity Koblitz chained-S3 line is closed at these parameters (verdict kill_high_arity_koblitz_line).
claims.if_not_supported: The line stays open (line_stays_open); a falsified K3 gives not_evaluable_instrument_invalid.

claims.text: No complete-DLP, end-to-end IC-versus-rho, leaderboard or benchmarks/README.md claim is in scope: the cells are relation-collection stage diagnostics and no matched rho is run.

positive.expected_detection: Every planted cell that completes inside its cap returns four witnesses of four, each re-added in the curve group and equal to the target (verified_relations = trials = 4, no proved_unsat). A planted cell that completes with a proved_unsat or an unverified witness is a miss: it invalidates that (m, n, S) cell's records. Planted cells that cap are unmeasured, not misses.

null_population.description: The m = 2 union:2 cell on each curve, a query the engine is known to decide (n83 record: chain-s3 decided 4/4 proved UNSAT at 17.3 s per query at n = 83).

factors.name: engine family and its domain
factors.value: two levels are crossed (see independent); everything else about the encoding is shared
factors.how: chain-s3 is the explicit-domain encoding the n83 record decided at m = 2; chain-s3-orbit is the signed-Frobenius orbit-domain encoding that capped there. Both read the same limits.

factors.name: trials
factors.value: 4 in Part A and the Part A negatives; 1 in Part B (liftB and the n83 negative)
factors.how: TRIALS is the grid trials column. Part B uses 1 so the 1800 s process cap is a per-query cap; Part A keeps 4 under a 600 s process cap, so a decided Part A cell is at most 150 s per query (factor-base time excluded). The n83 planted rows used 2 trials and the public rows 4, so Part B is not like-for-like with the record on trial count.

factors.name: seed and probe stream
factors.how: StdRng::seed_from_u64(seed ^ (m << 40)); the stream depends on m and the curve, not on S or engine. Same seed in every row, A/A included.

factors.name: per_query_ms
factors.how: Passed for the record; the chain engines do not read it. A query is bounded by conflict_budget 200000 and the process cap only.

factors.name: ChainS3Limits
factors.how: Compiled into the binary (examples/n83_msweep_cell.rs); the binary sha256 pins them.

factors.name: binary and commit
factors.how: One release binary of examples/n83_msweep_cell built once at the frozen commit; sha256 recorded at freeze and in every shard receipt.

factors.name: host class and threads
factors.value: one single-threaded process per cell; RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1
factors.how: isolab-eks native-L2 worker class; shards run concurrently on separate cores; host facts recorded per row.

factors.name: curve parameter a
factors.how: Fixed by the repository's curve aliases (src/cryptanalysis/curve_aliases.json has k0n23, k1n29, k0n31, k0n37, k0n41; no k0n29) and by the n83 record (known_n83_k1). a is confounded with n at n = 29 and n = 83, so C-n-scaling reads n across a mix of a values.

factors.name: cell_timeout_s
factors.how: Per cell process (timeout --kill-after=5). Part A: four trials share 600 s, so a decided cell has mean seconds per query at most 150 s. Part B: one trial per process, so 1800 s bounds one query.

factors.name: instance parity between modes
factors.how: public probes are [a]G for a drawn from the stream; planted probes are sums of m stream-chosen base points; the two modes are not matched targets.

factors.name: spot preemption and worker
factors.how: Worker, node and any interruption are recorded per row; an interrupted cell is discarded and re-run whole on an admitted worker.

comparisons.reason: At each (m, n, S): outcome class and seconds per decided query of chain-s3 versus chain-s3-orbit, ratio where both decide. Claims K1 to K6 are read per engine; this comparison reports the pair.

comparisons.threshold: Exact outcome per Part A cell, per engine: decided_sat, decided_unsat, decided_mixed, undecided or capped; K1 reads n = 23, K5 reads seconds per query against 188 s at n >= 31 (a decided cell is at most 150 s per query by the cap).
Exact outcome per Part B cell (one query, 1800 s cap), per engine; K4 needs all eight undecided or capped (four per engine), K5 reads seconds per query against 188 s.

comparisons.reason: Descriptive: seconds per decided query and outcome at m = 5 versus m = 6 at each (n, S); reported as a ratio where both decide, otherwise as the pair of outcomes. No claim is decided by it.
At fixed (m, S): log2 seconds per decided query against n across decided cells, and the first n at which the cell caps. a is 1 at n = 29 and 0 at the other Part A curves.

The 180 s record was run on another host and commit; only the cap is intended to differ. Read as a descriptive comparison of outcome (capped at 180 s versus decided or capped at 1800 s). The orbit union:2 m = 5, 6 cells have a 180 s record; orbit union:3 has none (the record's union:3 cells are chain-s3), so S = 3 is compared with chain-s3 union:3. Part B uses one trial per process while the record's public cells used four.

comparisons.threshold: Every planted cell that completes returns only verified witnesses (K3), per engine.

comparisons.reason: Identical arguments; outcome, relations, verified, base_points and columns must be identical; capped-versus-complete disagreement is a noise flag.

comparisons.threshold: Each m = 2 union:2 cell decides all four queries inside its cap; a cell that does not leaves the capped cells at that n uninformative about arity.

randomization.arm_order_reason: Each cell is its own process on its own core and the result is an exact outcome per cell; run order is ascending n within each m because the stopping rule reads the two previous curves, so it cannot be randomised. Shards (m = 2, 5, 6) run concurrently.

seed_derivation.note: The n83_msweep seed, reused unchanged in every cell and in the A/A duplicates; the binary derives each cell's stream as seed XOR (m << 40).

instance_sampling.rule: Four probes per cell from StdRng::seed_from_u64(8609517 ^ (m << 40)): public a uniform in 1..2^64 reduced modulo the subgroup order, target [a]G; planted a sum of m base points drawn by index from the factor base. The stream is a function of (seed, m, curve) and the mode, not of the engine or the factor-base span beyond the planted index range.

blinding.how: Outcomes are exact per cell and read against thresholds fixed in this protocol; there is no inferential comparison to mask.

power.note: Per-cell exact classification of four fixed queries; K1-K5 are threshold readings of exact cell outcomes, not sampled tests, so no power calculation applies. The one resolution limit: with four queries a cell's seconds per query is a mean over four, and the cap bounds it at cap/4 minus factor-base time for a decided cell. Part B has one query per cell.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Development preflight 2026-11-04T00:52-01:08Z, authoring VM (L0, no isolation, no /usr/bin/time), release binary sha256 in smoke/binary.sha256, frozen command lines, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Factor base union:2 at k0n23: 0.00012 s (fixed cost). Preflight cell (m = 5, k0n23, union:2, chain-s3-orbit, 4 trials): hit the 600 s process cap, no record written, so per_sample_seconds is the cap. Negative-control commands at m = 2 on the same curve and base: chain-s3 complete in 0.44 s, 4/4 proved_unsat, 0.108 s per query, 4727 conflicts; chain-s3-orbit complete in 191.3 s, 4/4 incomplete at the 200000-conflict budget, 47.8 s per query. The chained-S3 engines carry a conflict budget and no wall budget, so a query's wall time is bounded only by the process cap. Estimated total is the worst case with every cell at its cap (Part A 78000 s, Part B 32400 s); the stopping rule can only lower it. Peak RSS not measured here (no /usr/bin/time); the 8 GiB minimum stands as a placeholder.

primary.name: Cell decided
primary.definition: True iff the cell process exited 0 with a complete record and decided_fraction = 1 (every query of the cell (four in Part A, one in Part B) returned witness or proved_unsat). Classes: decided_sat (all witnesses), decided_unsat (all proved_unsat), decided_mixed, undecided (complete record, some query incomplete, unresolved, unsupported or invalid_model), capped (process_cap: killed at the cell cap), skipped_stopping_rule, process_error.

primary.name: Seconds per decided query
primary.definition: collection_seconds / trials for a decided cell (mean over its queries: four in Part A, one in Part B, factor-base construction excluded); not defined for capped or undecided cells, whose cap time is never reported as a cost. median_seconds_per_trial is carried as the spread.
primary.source: cell JSON seconds_per_trial, median_seconds_per_trial, collection_seconds, factor_base_seconds

secondary.name: SAT conflicts
secondary.definition: engine_work: the chained-S3 solver's conflict count summed over the cell's queries.

secondary.name: Chained SAT variables
secondary.definition: Variable count of the chained-S3 encoding at (m, n).
secondary.source: computed by analyze.py from m and the record's field_degree

secondary.name: Peak resident set
secondary.definition: GNU time maximum resident set of the cell process tree, from the <record>.time sidecar.

secondary.name: Process wall seconds
secondary.definition: Wall time of the whole cell process including factor-base construction; for capped cells the wall_seconds field of the process_cap record.

secondary.name: SAT models enumerated
secondary.definition: Not emitted by examples/n83_msweep_cell.rs (the record carries only the conflict total). Declared unavailable; no value is derived or imputed.

measurement.timed_primary_justification: The cost per decided query is the question's second half and it is a clock; the chained-S3 conflict count is carried as a counter but is not the price. Seconds are evidence only on isolab-eks with native L2, replay and A/A admission; any run on a lower tier, and the preflight, reports them as diagnostic. The decided/undecided split of a completed cell is a count and needs no isolation, but capped is a wall-clock event and shares the tier.

execution.queue: isolab-eks (cluster isolab, namespace isolab, us-east-2): cpu-l2-spot for the timed rows; one frozen_command card per shard (m = 2, 5, 6) via tools/task_card.py

placement.memory_note: Placeholder pending the preflight peak RSS; the chain encoding at m = 6, n = 83 has 105908 variables.
placement.campaign_usd_ceiling_note: To be set by the experiment director in the launch request before any spend (AGENTS.md section 9a); worst case 110400 CPU-seconds, about 30.7 vCPU-hours, plus build and idle.

stopping_rules.rule: Fixed grid: 148 cells in grid.tsv (Part A, both engines: 40 public + 40 planted + 40 A/A + 10 negative; Part B, both engines: 8 public + 8 planted + 2 negative), one fresh single-threaded process each, seed 8609517; 4 trials in Part A and 1 trial in Part B; cell caps 600 s (Part A, negatives at n <= 41) and 1800 s (Part B).
Per-cell cap: timeout --kill-after=5 at the cell cap; a killed cell is recorded as capped with its wall time and is never re-run with a longer cap.

Part A stopping rule, per m and per engine: curves run in the order k0n23, k1n29, k0n31, k0n37, k0n41; once all four public cells (S = 2, 3 at the two previous curves, same engine) are capped or skipped, every Part A cell of that m and engine (public, planted, A/A) at the next curve is recorded as skipped_stopping_rule and not run. Part B and the negatives are never skipped.

Invalidation stop: a failed positive control, a process_error, a binary sha256 different from the frozen one, or a negative-control cell that is process-capped (exit 124 or 137) or in process_error stops the affected shard for the director's assessment; no cap is changed. A negative-control cell that completes (exit 0) with queries the engine leaves undecided (verdict incomplete at its conflict budget) does not stop the shard: invalidation rule 4 applies per engine, and that engine's capped cells at that n are not_evaluable for K2 and K4.

invalidation_rules: A decided planted cell with a proved_unsat verdict or fewer than four verified witnesses invalidates the planted and public records of that (m, n, S) cell and the engine at it.
A decided public cell whose verified_relations differs from its relations (a witness that does not re-add to the target) is invalid.
An invalid_model verdict anywhere invalidates the cell.

A negative-control cell (m = 2, union:2) that does not decide all four queries inside its cap leaves the capped cells at that n uninformative about arity (reported as not_evaluable for K2 and K4); it does not by itself change any cap.

An A/A pair whose complete records differ in outcomes, relations, verified_relations, base_points or columns invalidates both records and halts the shard; one capped and one complete is a noise flag reported with the pair.
A binary whose sha256 differs from the frozen value, a source tree different from the frozen commit, or a worker without the L2 admission for a timed row makes its seconds diagnostic only.
A process_error (exit other than 0, 124, 137) is an invalid cell, not a cap.

decision_rule.text: Each cell receives one exact class (decided_sat, decided_unsat, decided_mixed, undecided, capped, skipped_stopping_rule, invalid_control, process_error). K1 to K5 are read per engine from those classes against the thresholds in the claims (K1: the two k0n23 union:2 public cells decide; K2: all m = 6 public cells at n = 37 and 41 capped and a positive log-slope between decided n; K3: every completed planted cell has only verified witnesses; K4: all four n83k1 public cells undecided or capped; K5: no decided public cell at n >= 31 under 188 s). Plainly on K5: Part A keeps TRIALS = 4 under a 600 s process cap, so a decided Part A cell proves at most 150 s per query and any decided Part A cell at n >= 31 falsifies K5 by construction; otherwise K5 stays untested on capped cells, because a cap is a censored observation and says nothing against 188 s. Only Part B (one query per process, 1800 s) can observe a per-query cost above 188 s. The kill criterion fires when, for both engines, K4 and K5 are supported and K3 is not falsified. A capped cell is never a cost.
decision_rule.threshold: Per cell: decided = every query of the cell decided inside the cap. Parity threshold 188 s per query (largest m = 4 root-table DLP of the n83 record). Observation caps: 600 s per Part A process (4 queries, so at most 150 s per query) and 1800 s per Part B process (1 query).
decision_rule.statistic: Exact per-cell outcome class and, for decided cells, mean and median seconds per query; ratio of seconds per decided query to 188 s as the distance from the m = 4 root-table parity point.
decision_rule.interval: No sampling interval; four fixed queries per cell, exact outcomes.
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: Seconds per decided query divided by 188 s (m = 4 root-table parity) and the m = 6 over m = 5 ratio; log2-slope of seconds per query in n at fixed (m, S).

graphs: Seconds per decided query against n for each (m, S), capped cells drawn as censored at the cap, with the 188 s parity line
Outcome grid: (m, S) by n, coloured by cell class, Part A and Part B

inadmissible: Raising, lowering or otherwise changing any cell cap after the freeze, or re-running a capped cell with a longer cap.
Changing the seed, trials, engine, factor-base span or ChainS3Limits after the freeze.
Reporting a capped cell, or the cap itself, as a cost or as a lower bound used for a projection.
Using the preflight smoke, its output or its seconds as evidence for any claim.
Reading seconds from a run without native L2 admission as timing evidence.
Reading a cell as informative about arity when its planted control missed or its negative control is undecided.
Presenting these relation-collection cells as a complete-DLP result, a leaderboard row or a speed-up over rho (K7).
Treating a Part A decided cell at n >= 31 as a pass without stating its distance to the 188 s parity point.
Reading a capped Part A cell as evidence that a query exceeds 188 s: four queries share the 600 s cap.

literature.claim: No measured m >= 5 cell exists with a Frobenius-invariant base; the m >= 5 half of the arity curve is unexplored.

Chained-S3 SAT at n = 83 decided only m = 2 (17.3 s per query, chain-s3) inside the 180 s cap; all m >= 3 chained cells capped; the m = 4 root-table complete DLPs took 175.2-188.5 s against strong rho 1.509 s.
literature.verified_by: README and table.tsv read on 2026-11-04; chain-s3-orbit union:2 m = 2 is process_cap in table.tsv.

literature.claim: Column format and the 180 s cell_timeout_s applied by run_shard.sh with timeout --kill-after=5.

Cell driver: sat_decompose_chained_s3_any_m with ChainS3Limits (4,000,000 variables; 50,000,000 domain clauses; 64 models; 200,000 conflicts); curve k<a>n<degree> via KoblitzCurve::new, n83k1 the pinned fixture; seed stream seed XOR (m << 40); the chain engines ignore per_query_ms.
Aliases k0n23, k1n29, k0n31, k0n37, k0n41 exist; k0n29 does not.

amendments.reason: The development preflight (sample_size.preflight_runtime.measured_on) found that the chain-s3-orbit engine leaves the m = 2 negative control undecided at its conflict budget on k0n23 (complete process, 4/4 incomplete), while chain-s3 decides it (4/4 proved_unsat). Stopping rule 4 read 'a negative control undecided at its cap' and did not say whether an undecided-but-complete control is a shard stop or the per-engine not_evaluable case of invalidation rule 4. Filed before the freeze and before any scientific cell.
